structure.overview: This case is a judicial review application by the Applicants challenging the Refugee Appeal Division's (RAD) decision dismissing their refugee appeal based on an Internal Flight Alternative (IFA) in Pakistan. The Applicants, Pakistani citizens who converted from Sunni to Shia Islam, argued that the RAD unreasonably assessed the risk of persecution by the Sunni extremist group SSP in the IFA. The Federal Court found the RAD's decision unreasonable for failing to properly consider uncontested evidence and country conditions, granting the judicial review application.

party_points.text: RAD erred in analyzing first prong of IFA test
RAD unreasonably required specific attack incidents in IFA
UNHCR says viable IFA generally unavailable to those targeted by armed militant groups
UNHCR identifies SSP as armed militant group
Requiring living in hiding in IFA is unreasonable

summaries.speaker: other
summaries.summary: This is a judicial review application under section 72 of IRPA of the RAD's December 21, 2021 decision dismissing the Applicants' refugee appeal.

citations.cite: Immigration and Refugee Protection Act, S.C. 2001, c 27
citations.why: Statutory basis for judicial review application

summaries.speaker: other
summaries.summary: The RAD did not doubt the following evidence presented by the Applicants.

summaries.speaker: other
summaries.summary: The Applicants are Pakistani citizens; the Principal Applicant (MA) was Sunni and converted to Shia in 2019, while his wife (FA) is Shia.

summaries.speaker: other
summaries.summary: After MA's 2019 conversion to Shia, Sunni extremists questioned him, which he did not deny.

summaries.speaker: other
summaries.summary: Anticipating problems after conversion, the Applicants applied for US visitor visas in August 2019.

summaries.speaker: other
summaries.summary: By late September 2019, the extremist Sunni group SSP learned of MA's conversion to Shia.

summaries.speaker: other
summaries.summary: MA was stopped and accosted by four armed men on his way home from work.

summaries.speaker: other
summaries.summary: The armed men threatened MA at gunpoint and physically assaulted him.

summaries.speaker: other
summaries.summary: The men demanded MA revert to Sunni faith or face death for being a traitor and infidel.

summaries.speaker: other
summaries.summary: MA reported the attack to police, who mocked him and registered the complaint without identifying attackers.

summaries.speaker: other
summaries.summary: The Applicants hid at a friend's house for weeks, who advised them to leave Pakistan.

summaries.speaker: other
summaries.summary: MA received a threatening call from someone claiming to be SSP after relocating.

summaries.speaker: other
summaries.summary: The caller said SSP knew of the police complaint and that the Applicants were targeted for killing.

summaries.speaker: other
summaries.summary: The Applicants fled to the US on visitor visas, then traveled to Canada and claimed refugee status in late 2019.

summaries.speaker: below
summaries.summary: The RAD relied on the RPD record and Pakistan country documents as the Applicants provided no new evidence.

summaries.speaker: below
summaries.summary: The RAD found no serious possibility of persecution or unreasonable relocation risk in the Internal Flight Alternative (IFA).

summaries.speaker: below
summaries.summary: The RAD applied the two-part Thirunavukkarasu test and found no serious persecution risk or unreasonable relocation in the IFA.

citations.cite: Thirunavukkarasu v Canada (Minister of Employment and Immigration), 1993 CanLII 3011 (FCA)
citations.why: Test applied by RAD to assess IFA viability

summaries.speaker: below
summaries.summary: The RAD found no evidence of targeted Shia violence in the IFA from country documents, so risk was not serious.

summaries.speaker: below
summaries.summary: The RAD assessed whether SSP had motivation and means to persecute the Applicants in the IFA beyond mere possibility.

summaries.speaker: below
summaries.summary: The RAD accepted SSP targets Shia groups and social gatherings traditionally.

summaries.speaker: below
summaries.summary: The RAD noted five 2019 Shia attacks but none in the IFA; UNHCR report lacked IFA-specific targeted attack info.

summaries.speaker: below
summaries.summary: The RAD held Applicants failed to prove SSP could locate them in the IFA despite police corruption; no added risk from police report.

summaries.speaker: below
summaries.summary: The RAD noted SSP searched Applicants' family home but not outside or via police or phone tracking.

summaries.speaker: below
summaries.summary: The RAD considered whether Applicants could safely travel to and live in the IFA without undue hardship.

summaries.speaker: below
summaries.summary: The RAD found MA's education and employment history support finding work in the IFA; language and religious practice possible; no systemic discrimination noted.

summaries.speaker: below
summaries.summary: The RAD found no evidence that MA's conversion history adds risk in Hyderabad, the IFA location.

summaries.speaker: below
summaries.summary: The RAD concluded the proposed IFA location is reasonable for the Applicants.

summaries.speaker: court
summaries.summary: The RAD and RPD accepted the Applicants' evidence; the issue is whether the RAD unreasonably found a viable IFA.

summaries.speaker: court
summaries.summary: The parties agree the applicable standard of review is reasonableness.

summaries.speaker: court
summaries.summary: Canada Post Corp v CUPW and Vavilov explain the requirements for a reasonable decision and judicial review under reasonableness.

citations.cite: Canada Post Corp v Canadian Union of Postal Workers, 2019 SCC 67
citations.why: Explains what constitutes a reasonable decision and judicial review under reasonableness

citations.cite: Canada (Minister of Citizenship and Immigration) v Vavilov, 2019 SCC 65
citations.why: Clarifies the reasonableness standard for judicial review

summaries.speaker: court
summaries.summary: The court explains that a reasonable decision must be coherent, rational, and justified by facts and law, citing Vavilov and related cases.

summaries.speaker: court
summaries.summary: The court states reasonableness depends on legal and factual context, requiring justification, transparency, and intelligibility, citing Vavilov and others.

citations.cite: Catalyst Paper Corp. v. North Cowichan (District), 2012 SCC 2, [2012] 1 S.C.R. 5, at para. 13

summaries.speaker: court
summaries.summary: The court explains the burden is on the challenger to prove the decision unreasonable by showing significant flaws, citing Vavilov.

citations.why: States burden on challenger to prove unreasonableness

summaries.speaker: party
summaries.summary: The Applicants argue the RAD correctly identified the IFA test but erred in analyzing the first prong and misinterpreted evidence.

summaries.speaker: party
summaries.summary: The Applicants contend the RAD unreasonably required specific attack incidents against Shia in the IFA despite evidence of widespread anti-Shia violence.

summaries.speaker: party
summaries.summary: The Applicants cite the UNHCR's conclusion that viable IFA is generally unavailable to those targeted by armed militant groups.

summaries.speaker: party
summaries.summary: The Applicants highlight a UNHCR footnote identifying the SSP as one such armed militant group.

summaries.speaker: court
summaries.summary: The court is not satisfied the RAD reasonably considered the UNHCR's conclusion that viable IFA is generally unavailable to those targeted by SSP.

summaries.speaker: court
summaries.summary: The court finds the RAD did not reasonably consider that the Applicants are specifically at risk from SSP, supported by uncontested evidence.

summaries.speaker: court
summaries.summary: The court concludes the RAD's risk assessment was unreasonable for failing to consider uncontested evidence and country conditions per Vavilov.

citations.why: Cited for instructions on reasonableness review

summaries.speaker: court
summaries.summary: The court finds the RAD's conclusion that SSP is unlikely to seek the Applicants outside their hometown unreasonable given evidence of ongoing threats.

summaries.speaker: party
summaries.summary: The Applicants argue, supported by Ali v Canada, that requiring them to live in hiding in the IFA is unreasonable.

citations.why: Supports Applicants' argument about living in hiding

summaries.speaker: court
summaries.summary: The court finds the RAD did not reasonably assess the risk of discovery by SSP in the IFA, endangering family and negating IFA status.

summaries.speaker: court
summaries.summary: The court notes other issues exist but will not consider them since judicial review is granted.

summaries.speaker: court
summaries.summary: The court concludes the RAD's decision was unreasonable and grants the application.

summaries.speaker: court
summaries.summary: The court states no question of general importance was proposed or arises.

summaries.speaker: court
summaries.summary: The court explains that internal rationality requires avoiding logical fallacies and ensuring the decision maker's reasoning is coherent.

summaries.speaker: court
summaries.summary: The court states a reasonable decision must be justified by relevant law and facts, citing Dunsmuir, Catalyst, and Nor-Man.

citations.why: Decision must be justified by law and facts

citations.cite: Nor-Man Regional Health Authority, at para. 6

summaries.speaker: court
summaries.summary: The court explains that reasonableness requires considering evidence and factual matrix, citing Dunsmuir, Southam, and Baker.

citations.why: Decision must be justified by facts
Unreasonableness if irrelevant stereotypes or ignoring evidence
